We are to implement the forward pass of the Outgoing Triangle Multiplicative Update (TriMul) operator as used in AlphaFold3 and related protein structure prediction models. The operator acts on a 4D tensor [B, N, N, C], but the implementation must be efficient enough to run on large N and hidden_dim.

The bottleneck for the TriMul operator is the reduction operation, which computes a new 4D tensor [B, N, N, H] by summing over the sequence index k. This is an O(N^3 * H) operation, but we can use a two-step reduction: first reduce over the sequence dimension k, then over the hidden dimensions. We will break down the problem into:

- Layer normalization
- Linear projections and gates (in FP16 for performance)
- Masking (if provided)
- Core reduction operation via tile-based approach
- Output normalization and gating

We will use a tile-based strategy where tiles will be configured to maximize shared memory usage and minimize register pressure. We will transpose the input tensor to [N, B, N, C] to spread out the batch dimension and allow for more efficient tiling. The tiled block will operate sequentially over the two sequence dimensions (i and j) and the hidden dimension (k), accumulating products on-the-fly.

- The dominant cost will be the N-shaped matrix multiplications (which will be 1024^2=1e6 elements per matrix initially, but we will tile to reduce this).
